title: Applied ML evals: Integration, Onboarding, Guardrails, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Priya Gupta
summary: Comprehensive playbook describing the end-to-end Applied ML evaluation lifecycle at Redwood: eval harness onboarding, prompt sets & benchmarks, model onboarding checklist, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and regression triage procedures.
content:
Overview

This playbook centralizes best practices for Applied ML evaluations at Redwood Inference. It is intended for ML engineers, applied researchers, platform engineers, and product owners involved in model onboarding, quality monitoring, and regression triage. The document covers:

- Eval harness onboarding and maintenance
- Prompt sets and benchmark creation
- Model onboarding checklist and acceptance criteria
- Quality guardrails and monitoring SLOs
- Quantization profile recommendations and testing matrix
- Regression triage runbook and escalation steps

Owners and roles

- Document owner: Applied ML (engineering)
- Primary contacts: Priya Gupta (Applied ML Lead), Ethan Brooks (Eval Infrastructure), Sofia Martinez (Model Reliability)
- On-call for regression triage: applied-ml-incident rotation (see eng-sre/runbooks)

1) Eval harness: onboarding and standards

Goal: Provide a reproducible, automated harness that runs model-level evaluations (unit, behavioral, and production-sim) and integrates into CI/CD and nightly pipelines.

Minimum requirements for a model to be added to the eval harness:
- Model artifact and manifest (model_id, version, framework, quantization support)
- Container or artifact with deterministic entrypoint (command + args)
- Example inference script and small sample dataset (<=100 examples)
- Declared expected tokenization and sequence-length distribution
- Eval config YAML in repo: includes prompt set references, metrics to compute, and resource hints

CI integration checklist:
1. Add model eval job to the shared eval pipeline (Jenkins/GitHub Actions template).
2. Ensure reproducible seed usage for stochastic metrics.
3. Configure thresholds and alerts in the eval job (see Alerting section).
4. Add a nightly full-run entry with larger prompt sets for drift detection.

Example eval config (YAML snippet):

---
model_id: rl-model-v2
version: 2026-10-01
prompt_sets:
  - id: core-instructions-v1
  - id: safety-and-toxic-v1
metrics:
  - exact_match
  - rouge_l
  - toxicity_score
seed: 42
resource_hints: "g4dn.xlarge"
thresholds:
  rouge_l: 0.65
  toxicity_score: 0.03
---

2) Prompt sets and benchmarks

Principles for prompt set creation:
- Coverage: include representative traffic (intent diversity, lengths, tokens, edge-cases).
- Partition: split into smoke (fast, ~100 samples), regression (1k-5k), and production-sim (10k+) sets.
- Ownership: each prompt set must have a single named owner and a changelog.
- Privacy: remove or obfuscate any customer PII; classify sets as public/internal/restricted.

Prompt set metadata fields (required): id, owner, intended_use, size, privacy_classification, created_at, last_updated, tags.

Benchmark creation process:
1. Define the user-facing behavior to test (e.g., summarization accuracy for long documents).
2. Collect human-labeled references where possible; use crowd labels for subjective tasks with clear instructions.
3. Split sets into train/validation/test where applicable.
4. Define automated metric(s) and human-review triggers for low-confidence cases.
5. Publish results to the eval dashboard with timestamped runs and model versions.

3) Model onboarding checklist and acceptance criteria

Minimum acceptance criteria before a model is eligible for serving:
- Safety checks: no high-risk failure modes on safety prompt sets (toxicity, personal data leakage).
- Performance: meets baseline latency (p50/p95) and throughput targets on the serving profile for the deployment class. See performance-standards for hardware-specific targets.
- Quality: passes regression prompt set thresholds (see example thresholds below).
- Cost profile: estimated token cost and memory footprint validated against quantization recommendations.
- Observability: exposes metrics (tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, cache_hit_rate) and traces compatible with Redwood Console.
- Documentation: model card + quantization notes + known limitations and recommended use-cases.

Example quality thresholds (illustrative):
- Summarization ROUGE-L >= 0.62 on regression set
- Code generation pass@1 >= 0.58 on code-bench
- Toxicity mean <= 0.03 on safety set

Deployment gating flow:
1. Eval team verifies harness results and signs off on thresholds.
2. Platform schedules a canary rollout (5-10% traffic) with increased logging.
3. After 72 hours and no regressions, proceed to gradual ramp to target capacity.

4) Quality guardrails and monitoring SLOs

Guardrails we enforce in production:
- Safety SLOs: <= 0.05% high-severity safety violations per 1M requests (monitored via sampling + classifier).
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 600ms for hosted small models, p95 <= 1200ms for large models (dedicated targets defined per fleet).
- Regression detection: any metric drop > 5% relative to baseline on regression set triggers automated rollback evaluation.

Monitoring configuration requirements:
- Sampling rate: 1% of requests captured for behavioral evals, 100% of failed requests.
- Logging: include prompt hash, model_version, route_id, latency_ms, and anonymized response features for downstream evals.
- Alerts: PagerDuty for critical safety/regression alerts; Slack for informative degradations.

5) Quantization profiles and testing matrix

Profiles: we maintain a set of quantization profiles per model family and target hardware. A profile includes: algorithm (PTQ/QAT), bitwidth (8-bit, 4-bit), calibration dataset id, and tolerance thresholds for accuracy.

Quantization testing matrix (example):
- Family: llama-2-13b
  - FP16 baseline (baseline run)
  - PTQ 8-bit (calibration set: quant-cal-1k) -> allowed accuracy loss: <= 1.5% relative
  - PTQ 4-bit (calibration set: quant-cal-5k) -> allowed accuracy loss: <= 3.5% relative
  - QAT 4-bit (if available) -> allowed accuracy loss: <= 1.0% relative

Quantization validation procedure:
1. Run baseline eval on regression prompt set and record metrics.
2. Apply quantization profile and run identical eval.
3. Compare metrics; if any metric loss exceeds profile tolerance, mark profile as failed and do not route traffic to quantized variant.
4. Document any failure modes in the quantization profile changelog and raise for model/infra review.

CLI example to run quantization validation:

# run baseline
python -m eval_harness.run --model rl-model-v2 --config eval-config.yaml --out baseline.json
# run quantized
python -m eval_harness.run --model rl-model-v2-ptq8 --config eval-config.yaml --out ptq8.json

6) Regression triage and incident playbook

Objective: efficiently detect, triage, and remediate quality regressions introduced by model changes, infra updates, or data drift.

Detection triggers:
- Scheduled nightly regression job fails thresholds
- Production sampling shows metric drop > configured relative threshold (default 5%)
- Safety classifier flags increase in high-severity events

Immediate triage steps (first 30 minutes):
1. Owner on-call acknowledges the alert and creates a triage incident in the incident tracker.
2. Pull the last successful eval run and the failing run artifacts (config, model_id, metrics).
3. Reproduce locally with the same seed and config; if unreproducible, increase sample and annotate nondeterminism.

Root cause investigation checklist (first 4 hours):
- Model change: did the model binary or weights change? Check git tag and build manifest.
- Promptset change: were prompts updated or re-labeled? Compare prompt set commits.
- Quantization/infra change: was a quantized variant deployed or a new runtime kernel enabled?
- Data drift: compare request distribution (tokens, route mix) to baseline.
- Resource contention: check GPU utilization and OOM/retry logs.

Mitigation options (ordered by safety and speed):
1. Rollback model version to last-known-good; initiate emergency canary rollback if in production.
2. Disable quantized variant routing and route to FP16 baseline.
3. Apply prompt filters or input sanitization as short-term fix for safety failures.
4. Patch model with targeted prompt/behavioral fixes and run fast validation.

Escalation policy:
- If safety-critical regression (e.g., data leakage, high-sev toxicity): page Security Lead and Applied ML Director immediately; set P0.
- If regression persists > 24 hours without mitigation, schedule cross-functional incident review and freeze new model rollouts.

Post-incident: postmortem and prevention
- Owner writes a blameless postmortem within 3 business days including timeline, RCA, and action items.
- Required follow-ups: expanded test coverage, improved sampling or new prompt sets, and automation to prevent recurrence.

7) Dashboards, alerts, and reporting

Key dashboards to maintain:
- Regression dashboard: model vs baseline metric deltas over time by prompt set and route
- Safety dashboard: sampled safety incidents, severity trend, and top offending prompts
- Quantization dashboard: variant-level metrics and accuracy delta plots

Alerting thresholds (examples):
- Regression: relative drop > 5% on primary metric for two consecutive nightly runs -> PagerDuty (on-call)
- Safety: absolute increase of +0.01 mean toxicity on safety set over baseline -> PagerDuty + Security Slack channel
- Latency: p95 > SLO for 15 min -> Ops Slack channel and paged if > 30 min

8) Governance and reviews

- Quarterly eval review: applied-ml presents top regressions, new prompt sets, and quantization changes to the ML Platform and Product stakeholders.
- Model cards: every onboarded model must include a model card published in the model registry and linked in the eval dashboard.
- Change control: changes to prompt sets and quantization profiles require at least one reviewer from Security (for safety-sensitive sets) and one from Platform (for infra-impacting changes).
